verdict.corrective_finite_result: Retaining a common dyadic factor(1+|u0|)^(-1) yields a rigorous finite resonance bound. Summed over signed dyadic h blocks, R_decay <=8192*T*(1+log(2S))*V*U^2/Q, where T=max_{1<=w<=floor(4RS)}tau(w). Also |O|<=64*T*U^2*R^2*S.

Original kappa<=sigma/100 leaves a resonance-only power margin; no smaller-kappa premise is needed.
verdict.status_limit: The finite inequalities and decay-envelope proof route here are mathematical, not formalized. Existing Envelope313d has NO u0-decay conclusion. Nonresonant/root/spectral7/32 estimates, exact full operator assembly, C/K,hLower,hUpper remain OPEN.

notation.dyadic_blocks: For ell>=0 set H_ell=2^ell and I_ell^epsilon={h in Z:sign(h)=epsilon,H_ell<=|h|<2H_ell}, with epsilon=+,-; intersect each row's exact H_D window. These blocks partition all nonzero h up to H_1 exactly, with no h=0 and no endpoint multiplicity.

counterexample.family: Take integer n→infinity (even n may be used), U=n,V=n^3,X=n^4,Q=R=S=1,residue a=n^4,B=0,sigma=1/1000,kappa=0,c0=1. Choose intervalLo=n-1,intervalHi=2n; alpha identically0; beta=1 on original betaCarrier and0 elsewhere; gamma_i(q)=1 ifq=1 and0 otherwise.
counterexample.admissibility: For large n: X>exp(exp1),|a|=X exactly;1<n^(1-4sigma);U^2=n^2<n^(4-32sigma);|a|^(7/32)U=n^(15/8)<n^(8-60sigma);U^(1+7/16)=n^(23/16)<n^(8-60sigma). Coefficient norm/coprimality gates hold because active factor1 is coprime to a. Rough-alpha gate is vacuous and UniformAuxiliarySW is identically zero. This is a genuinely admissible family for the original parameters, though its actual alpha-weighted sum is zero.
counterexample.outer_subset: Take p=r=rprime=sprime=D=1 and every ordered N1,N2 in{n,...,2n},N1!=N2. There are n(n+1) such pairs. Each lies in O, gcd(r*1,rprime*sprime)=1=D, and CRT compatibility for q=qprime=1 holds automatically. No choice of a or inverse phase can change the unit norm of K_o(1,1).
counterexample.single_common_coefficients: Use lambda_s=1_{s=1},omega_h=1_{h=1}, common to every outer row. Then each selected row has one nonzero bare inner entry, so its sole nonzero unsigned-slope fibre has squared modulus1. A_o=V=n^3, hence R_bare>=V^2*n(n+1) and |O|>=n(n+1).
counterexample.ceil_and_true_profile: Choose any fixed0<eta<3/4, including arbitrarily small eta allowed by the route. Then Z=n^(4eta), and for sufficiently large n,0<64 Z/V<=1, so H_1=1. Thus h=1 is in the EXACT source window, not an artificial enlarged window. But the actual lowpass at s=1 has argument V/Z=n^(3-4eta)>=2 and is zero. The true smooth row contributions of this subset vanish.
counterexample.outside_lower_bound: Original betaCarrier={n^3,...,2n^3}, so its beta energy is n^3+1. The original gamma1 energy is1. Hence E_out=n^3+1 and E_out*sqrt(|O|*R_bare)>=(n^3+1)*n^3*n(n+1)>=n^8=X^2. Any uniform O(X^2/log(X)^A),A>0, bound for this bare expression is false, even BEFORE multiplying the nondecaying envelope mass.
counterexample.O_versus_C_warning: The source outer coefficient C_o contains cleaned transposed beta=cleaned alpha, hence C_o=0 in this family. The source's upper bound sum|C_o|^2<=|O| discards this information. The paired-gcd/supported-part Y gates also live in C_o and are discarded in O. Therefore the counterexample refutes precisely the OVERSTRONG coefficient-discarded bare endpoint proposed for O; it does not claim these are nonzero original coefficient rows, nor that all Y gates hold for every selected pair.
counterexample.no_stronger_claim: No lower bound with retained Y gates or nonzero rough alpha density is asserted. Obtaining such a different counterexample would require a separate density argument and is unnecessary to refute the actual coefficient-discarded bare endpoint. Original theorem and exact C/K constants are untouched.

finite_fibre_count.exact_identity: For positive integer s,t and integer H>=0, the number of signed nonzero h,k with|h|,|k|<=H and|h|/s=|k|/t equals4*floor(H*gcd(s,t)/max(s,t)). Write s=g*s1,t=g*t1 with(s1,t1)=1: |h|=j*s1,|k|=j*t1,1<=j<=H/max(s1,t1),and choose the two signs independently.
finite_fibre_count.bound: For s,t in the integer interval[S,2S], total count P(H,S)<=16 H S*(1+log(2S)). Proof: floor<=argument,max(s,t)>=S,gcd(s,t)<=sum_{d|s,d|t}d. There are at most floor(2S/d)<=2S/d multiples of d in the interval. Hence sum_{s,t}gcd(s,t)<=4S^2*sum_{d<=floor(2S)}1/d<=4S^2*(1+log(2S)). Multiply by4H/S.
finite_fibre_count.block_version: A signed dyadic block has|h|<2H_ell, so using the larger window gives P<=32 H_ell S L_S. The sum of the two separate same-sign fibre counts is at most this full signed count. Original masks only delete pairs; triangle inequality and |lambda|,|omega|,|K|<=1 make this valid for arbitrary common complex sequences and phases.
finite_fibre_count.why_plain_sum_A_squared_bad: The coarse formula R_bare<=16 S L_S sum_o H_D A_o^2 is mathematically true, but by itself loses positive D factors and the small-frequency amplitude. H_D includes a+1 ceiling term. The counterexample shows no sharper treatment of gcd counts alone can make the unweighted bare endpoint uniformly logarithmically small.

exact_outer_counts.offdiagonal_progression_count: For fixed positive integer m, the number of ordered distinct N1,N2 in[U,2U] with N1 congruent N2 mod m is <=4U^2/m. There are<=U+1<=2U choices forN1; each nonzero difference is a signed multiple of m of absolute value<=U, giving at most2floor(U/m)<=2U/m choices. Crucially there is no additive+1 because N1=N2 is excluded.
exact_outer_counts.O_card: In O use m=p. Sum_p1/p<=2 on[Q,2Q], and there are<=8R^2S triples(r,rprime,sprime). Every w=rprime*sprime<=4RS has<=T divisors. Therefore |O|<=4U^2*2*8R^2S*T=64 T U^2R^2S.
exact_outer_counts.active_rows: Let Ostar={o in O:pD divides N1-N2}. Every nonzero K row lies here by exact CRT compatibility and the gcd=D mask. Using m=pD, count N pairs<=4U^2/(pD). This positivity restriction is used before summing D; replacing it by only mod p loses the needed cancellation.
exact_outer_counts.mesh_first_moment: For fixed p,r,rprime,sprime,D, count*Nmesh <=[4U^2/(pD)]*[VD/(p*r*S*rprime*sprime)]=4VU^2/(p^2*r*S*rprime*sprime). D cancels EXACTLY. Summing D costs only T, not sumD or maxD. Use sum_p1/p^2<=2/Q, sum_r1/r<=2,sum_rprime1/rprime<=2,sum_sprime1/sprime<=2 to get sum_{o in Ostar}A_o<=64 T VU^2/(Q S).
exact_outer_counts.mask_scope: Dropping the remaining gcd and coprimality restrictions in these positive upper bounds is harmless. They remain in the defined kernel; no arbitrary-mask cancellation theorem is inferred. The bounds also hold if actual Y/coefficient support restrictions are retained, since those only shrink the positive sums.

normalization_and_original_range.number_of_blocks: Let L_H be the number of dyadic absolute-h blocks intersecting[1,H_1]. Then there are at most2L_H signed blocks. A Cauchy bound on the sum of their square-root resonance bounds costs sqrt(2L_H), not a power ofH_1.
normalization_and_original_range.combined_bound: Let M_R=C_env*(1+Rphase)^4 be the common remaining envelope mass after retaining decay. The resonance-only contribution to the quantity E_out*sqrt(CauchyMass) is bounded by E_out*sqrt(|O|)*M_R*sqrt(2L_H)*sqrt(sum R_ell,epsilon). Using the exact constants above yields <=4096*C_env*T*L_B*sqrt(L_H*L_S)*(1+Rphase)^4 * U^2*V^(3/2)*Q^(1/2)*R*S^(1/2). Here4096=4*sqrt(64*8192*2).
normalization_and_original_range.ratio: Divide byX^2=U^2V^2: <=4096*C_env*T*L_B*sqrt(L_H*L_S)*(1+Rphase)^4*sqrt(QR^2S/V). WithN1>=U, Rphase=X^kappa is valid for the fixed-row log family. SinceX>=1,kappa>=0,(1+Rphase)^4<=16X^(4kappa).
normalization_and_original_range.geometry: Q<U X^(-sigma) and U^2SR^2<X^(1-8sigma)=UV X^(-8sigma) imply QR^2S/V <X^(-9sigma). Therefore the only new power in the normalized resonance estimate is X^(-9sigma/2+4kappa), before divisor/log factors.
normalization_and_original_range.eta_and_logs: For fixed eta>0, H_1=ceil(64X^eta QR^2S^2/V). UsingQ<=U andU^2R^2S<X gives QR^2S^2/V<S<=X; hence H_1<=1+64X^(eta+1), soL_H=O_eta(1+logX). AlsoS,V<=X. Thus all L_H,L_S,L_B are fixed logarithmic powers. No smallness condition on eta is needed for THIS corrected resonance bound; eta restrictions from other pieces remain separate.
normalization_and_original_range.divisor_subpower: SinceR,S>=1 andU^2SR^2<X,4RS<=4X. The standard elementary divisor subpower bound therefore givesT<=C_delta X^delta for every fixeddelta>0. This audit does not claim a newly compiled divisor lemma; its required scope is only the actual finite maximum up to4X, not a new spectral estimate.
normalization_and_original_range.original_kappa: For0<=kappa<=sigma/100, -9sigma/2+4kappa<=-4.46sigma. For example choosing divisor exponentdelta=sigma/2 and absorbing all fixed logarithmic factors in anotherX^(sigma/2) leaves exponent at most-3.46sigma. Thus, AFTER proving the retained-decay envelope and formal finite bridges, this resonance component has enough margin for every prescribed log saving under the unchanged original parameter range.

normalization_and_original_range.not_full_operator_bound: This bound pays the NEW decay-weighted positive resonance only. The bare/decay-weighted nonresonant form, root operators, coefficient separation and spectral7/32 estimate have not been proved. No assumption asserting them is added.
